raw.query: WITH ranked AS (SELECT resolution, variate, model, ROUND(AVG(mae)::numeric, 2) AS avg_mae, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY resolution, variate ORDER BY AVG(mae)) AS rnk FROM forecast_metrics WHERE candidate = 'point' GROUP BY resolution, variate, model) SELECT resolution, variate, model, avg_mae, rnk FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 2 ORDER BY resolution, variate, rnk
raw.observed: 1s: toto wins all 4 variates (gaps 0.8-2.9%); 15s: toto wins 2/4, chronos wins 2/4; 30s: toto wins 3/4; 45s: chronos wins 2/4, timesfm wins 1/4; 1min: timesfm wins 2/4, toto wins 2/4. Winner shifts across resolutions AND variates. Top-2 gaps: 0.12-4.72% of MAE.
raw.claimed: "which model wins is resolution-dependent, and the inter-model ranking is noise-level"
raw.evidence: Toto dominates at 1s (4/4 variates), but at 15s+ the winner varies by variate (toto, chronos, timesfm split wins); top-2 gaps never exceed 4.7% of MAE, confirming noise-level differences.
raw.fix: At 1s toto is consistently #1 across all variates (gaps 0.8-2.9%), which is the one resolution where ranking is NOT purely noise — could note this as a caveat.
